slides.title: Conversation control
slides.subtitle: Sign in mid-conversation, talk directly, hand off to a person, close
slides.notes: A conversation is more than messages. This example drives one Manzanita conversation through four controls: signing in part-way through, a Direct Conversation, a handoff to a person at the support desk, and closing.

slides.title: Who takes part

columns.heading: Ada
columns.content: The user. She signs in on Manzanita's page and asks to talk to the company herself.

columns.heading: Atlas
columns.content: Her personal agent. Its host holds the tokens and drives the conversation.

columns.heading: Manzanita
columns.content: The company, with a support desk staffed for the handoff.

slides.notes: Ada is the user, Atlas is her personal agent, and Manzanita is the company. In this example Manzanita has people at its support desk, so a handoff can be taken.

slides.title: Sign-in mid-conversation

items.title: Ask
items.detail: Where is my jacket order? Signed out

slides.notes: Signed out, Manzanita cannot look up an order, so it answers with an authorization event: sign_in_required and the scopes it needs. The host signs Ada in with a mode the company offers, here device sign-in, and keeps sending to the same conversation ID with the new token.

slides.title: A Direct Conversation
slides.notes: Only the personal agent starts a Direct Conversation, so the user can talk with the company in the agent's own interface. While it is open, the parent refuses messages and handoff with direct_conversation_open, and the SDK puts the open conversation's ID in the error details.

slides.title: Handoff, then close

items.title: handoff()
items.detail: Ask for a person at the company

slides.notes: A handoff puts the conversation in the queued state until a person takes it; then the responder is human. When nobody is available, the company says so and the agent carries on. Closing ends the conversation, but operations it proposed or started are not cancelled.

slides.title: The four controls

rows.label: Sign-in (§7.11)
values: The company, with an authorization event

slides.notes: Here are the four side by side. Each comes back to the model as an event type, a status or an error code it can explain to the user.

slides.title: What stays where

left.heading: Host-only
items: The user code, shown by the host

slides.notes: The model sees what happened, never the means. Tokens, the device code and proofs stay in the host, and the user code is shown to the user by the host, not by the model.

slides.title: Run it yourself
slides.cta: The Pydantic AI and Agent Runtimes examples drive one Manzanita conversation through all four
slides.notes: Run the Pydantic AI example with PAP_EXAMPLE_MODEL set to the model you want. TypeScript has startDirect, handoff and close on ConversationClient, with the same error codes and details.
